dedupe_keys.name: mining concessions global forest watch land carbon lab v2025

description: This WRI layer aggregates national mining concession data into one global map of areas allocated by governments or other bodies for mineral extraction. "Concession" is used for licences, permits, tenures and other contracts that give companies rights to explore or extract minerals. The 2025 version covers Brazil, Cambodia, Cameroon, Canada, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Indonesia, Mexico, Malaysia, Peru, the Republic of the Congo, Suriname and Zambia, with sources from government agencies, NGOs and other organisations whose dates vary, and includes only active or available concessions as defined by each source. It is a shapefile download free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, updated as needed; the entry was created in July 2026. Caveats: the provider says quality varies by source, a country's layer may not include all concessions and some locations may be inaccurate; the Colombia data from Tierra Minada include special zones such as for Indigenous groups. For simulation it shows where mining rights overlap forests, protected areas, rivers and infrastructure corridors, useful for land-use conflict, deforestation and supply expansion scenarios. Related catalogue records include the NRCan principal mineral areas map, the IPIS artisanal mining data and the Global Coal Mine Tracker.
